agentContributions.notes: Novel capability: Contentstack Live Preview integration. The central attachment point is useContent (236 callers) — every Contentstack component flows through getContentByKey. Live Preview must plug into this hook to inject draft/preview content into the existing rendering pipeline without changing downstream components. Secondary attachment: the Contentstack SDK client initialization/provider where the Live Preview SDK must be configured with preview tokens and host. No acceptance criteria were provided; VCs derived from the description.

Openspec produced zero acceptance criteria, so all criteria are original to this review. I derived them from the story title (Live Preview of Content in CMS), openspec's notes identifying useContent (236 callers) and Contentstack SDK client as attachment points, and the listed files. Key areas covered: (1) happy-path real-time preview rendering (AC-1), (2) no-op fallback when unconfigured (AC-2), (3) transparency to downstream consumers (AC-3), (4) type/shape stability (AC-4), (5) network error degradation (AC-5), (6) token expiry handling (AC-6), (7) security — no token leakage in prod builds (AC-7), (8) concurrent entry independence (AC-8), (9) ContentstackLink integrity (AC-9), (10) accessibility preservation (AC-10), (11) non-blocking initialization (AC-11), (12) clean disconnect behavior (AC-12). CAVEAT: I have not seen the contents of the four referenced files; criteria are based on paths and story context alone. If useContent or the Contentstack SDK client have existing error-handling or caching patterns, some criteria may need refinement to align with those patterns.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. OpenSpec provided strong architectural analysis — identifying useContent (236 callers) as the central attachment point and the Contentstack SDK client as the secondary integration point, with a clear strategy for injecting preview content without downstream changes. Speckit then derived 12 comprehensive acceptance criteria from OpenSpec's notes, covering happy-path rendering, fallback behavior, security (token leakage), error degradation, concurrency, and cleanup. The division of labor was complementary (architecture vs. testable criteria). However, Speckit explicitly flagged that it had not seen the contents of the four referenced files, meaning all 12 ACs were derived blind from paths and story context alone. If useContent or the Contentstack SDK client have existing error-handling, caching, or initialization patterns, some criteria may not align. A human should validate the derived ACs against the actual codebase before implementation proceeds.
